section.p: Shaping the Future of Research Assessment: A Canadian Strategy is a national workshop bringing together key collaborators from across Canada's research community to advance implementation of responsible research assessment (RRA) at scale. Hosted by the University of Victoria on June 8–10, 2027, the workshop will explore how research quality, contributions, and impact can be evaluated through more transparent, equitable, and inclusive approaches.

Although support for responsible research assessment continues to grow, many Canadian institutions face challenges translating these principles into practical policies and practices. The Future of Research Assessment aims to bridge the gap between commitment and implementation by fostering collaboration, knowledge sharing, and developing actionable strategies to synergize how research is assessed and recognized across Canada.

The workshop will bring together researchers, artists, graduate students, university leaders, research administrators, librarians, funders, publishers, policy professionals, and community partners. By connecting individuals from diverse disciplines, institutions, and career stages, the event will encourage meaningful dialogue and collaboration across Canada's research ecosystem and support implementation across diverse institutional settings and contexts.

Through plenary presentations, panel discussions, roundtables, and collaborative exercises, participants will identify common challenges, exchange best practices, and develop practical solutions for advancing responsible research assessment.

A key outcome will be the development of The Victoria Standard for Implementing Research Assessment in Canada: A National Strategy, which will be made available open access in both English and French. This document is intended to be a national framework providing guidance for implementing responsible research assessment across Canadian institutions. The workshop will also lead to the development of open access resource hub and help establish a national community of practice dedicated to supporting meaningful, sustainable change in research assessment.
